title: Digital Logic Design
description: Digital and analogue signals, data representation and signed numbers, binary codes and error detection, logic gates and their properties, Boolean algebra and the canonical forms, Karnaugh maps and combinational design (adders, subtractors and comparators), and sequential circuits, flip-flops, registers and counters. Built from the IFT 211 lecture slides in the course folder's 'arranged' set (1 to 9) and the Tarnoff chapters filed with them.

topics.title: Digital Signals and Data Representation
topics.summary: Digital signals are discrete in value and time, unlike continuous analogue signals, and digital systems represent all data in binary. Signed integers are stored in sign-magnitude, 1's complement or 2's complement form, and real numbers can use a fixed-point form.
subtopics: Features and advantages of digital systems
Data, information and the four functions of a computer

topics.title: Binary Codes and Error Detection
topics.summary: Binary codes represent decimal digits (BCD and other weighted or non-weighted codes) and characters (ASCII, EBCDIC, Unicode). Errors in transmission are single-bit or burst errors; parity checks detect them and Hamming codes also correct them.
subtopics: Alphanumeric codes: ASCII, EBCDIC and Unicode

topics.title: Logic Gates and Their Properties
topics.summary: Logic gates are built from transistors and described by a truth table, a logic symbol and a Boolean expression. NAND and NOR are universal gates; logic families are compared by noise immunity, noise margin, fan-in and fan-out.
subtopics: Noise, noise immunity and noise margin

topics.title: Boolean Algebra and Standard Forms
topics.summary: Boolean algebra manipulates binary variables with AND, OR and NOT to simplify functions. Its identities come in dual pairs, and any function can be written in canonical form as a sum of minterms or a product of maxterms.
subtopics: Binary variables and the three basic operations
Literals, product terms and sum terms

topics.title: Karnaugh Maps and Combinational Design
topics.summary: Karnaugh maps simplify Boolean functions graphically by grouping adjacent cells that differ in one variable. Combinational design moves from a description to a truth table, expression and simplified circuit, and gives adders, subtractors and comparators.
subtopics: Half adder, overflow and carry look-ahead

topics.title: Sequential Circuits, Counters and Registers
topics.summary: Sequential circuits use feedback and storage, so their outputs depend on present and past inputs. Latches and flip-flops (SR, JK, D and T) store bits; registers move and store binary vectors and counters cycle through 2ⁿ states.
subtopics: SR, JK, D and T flip-flops
Asynchronous counters, modulus and frequency division
